title: Accuracy in Wrist-Worn, Sensor-Based Measurements of Heart Rate and Energy Expenditure in a Diverse Cohort (Shcherbina et al. 2017)
content: Shcherbina A et al., 2017 — Evaluated several wrist-worn consumer devices against reference standards for heart rate and energy expenditure. Devices measured heart rate reasonably well, but energy-expenditure (calorie burn) estimates carried substantially larger errors across all tested devices and activities. Wrist-worn calorie-burn figures should not be treated as ground truth.

title: Accuracy in Wrist-Worn, Sensor-Based Measurements of Heart Rate and Energy Expenditure in a Diverse Cohort (Shcherbina et al. 2017)
content: Shcherbina et al. 2017 — Product implication: a wearable's reported 'calories burned' figure should be labeled and treated internally as an ESTIMATE of active energy expenditure, not an exact number. Nutrition logic should never default to automatically adding 100% of a wearable's reported calorie burn back onto a user's intake target — doing so compounds the device's real measurement error into the prescription itself.
